newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, HSFO still supported.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, HSFO still supported.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Friday in sluggish trade, with grades in the U.S. Gulf, particularly high sulphur, still firm in the face of ongoing heat in Florida and some buying interest for Mexico.
"The fundamentals on the Gulf are still pretty good with Florida (utilities) burning and people looking to cover commitments to Mexico," said one cash trader.
But traders agreed New York Harbor was not well supported, with little extreme heat in the area and cheap city gate gas prices still siphoning demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped about a dime to the $16.50-75 a barrel area, still undermined by mild weather and fuel switching to gas.
NYH August one percent paper was quoted little changed on the day in the $16.25-30 area, with September paper still straddling $16, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour stumbled more than a quarter to about $17.75 on soft utility demand.
New York high sulphurs again held steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted in the low-$15s.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent again was unchanged in the low-$16 area, while three percent moved up a quarter to $14.25-50, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices inched up a penny or two Friday to about the $2.40/mmBtu level, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was up slightly to $2.16/mmBtu, or $13.61 a barrel.
